title: Lean 4 Resolution of Erdős Problems #593 and #1177 on Obligatory Hypergraph Triple Systems
whyItMatters: Completely classifies all obligatory finite 3-uniform hypergraphs (#593, $500 prize) and resolves all three clauses of #1177 in a zero-sorry Lean 4 formalization co-authored with Harmonic Aristotle.
summary: Eric Li (Trinity College, University of Cambridge), collaborating with Harmonic’s Aristotle theorem prover (explicitly co-authored in the Lean 4 repository), unconditionally resolved Erdős Problem #593 ($500 prize, posed by Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal) and all three sub-questions of Erdős Problem #1177 (truth values: yes, no, yes). The proof proves an exact bridge-trace theorem for complete-rank one-apex sequence lifts, characterizing obligatory finite triple systems in uncountably chromatic 3-uniform hypergraphs, with every theorem machine-checked in Lean 4 (zero sorry, standard axioms, independently replayed across 8,091 jobs).
technicalHighlights: Exact characterization of Erdős #593 ($500 prize): a finite triple system (sans isolated vertices) is obligatory iff it is linear, every hyperedge-node of its Levi graph has an incident bridge, and every Berge cycle is even.
Establishes a class-valued exact avoidance-spectrum dichotomy settling all three clauses of Erdős #1177 (yes, no, yes).
100% formalized in Lean 4 with Harmonic Aristotle (zero sorry, standard axioms) and independently replayed across 8,091 build jobs.
caveats: Published as an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2606.24882v2) and public Lean 4 repository rather than a peer-reviewed journal article, though independently kernel-replayed in Lean 4.
